quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to protect your hands.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed
So your legs can absorb the shock
So other drivers can see you better
So you can see the uneven surface better

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs and joints absorb some of the impact. This helps prevent the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can greatly reduce head injury severity
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head injury severity
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet while riding greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious head or neck injury in a crash. A DOT-approved helmet will not block your side vision.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and brightly-colored clothing at all times when riding a motorcycle. Crashes happen during the day and at night, so wear highly visible clothing any time you ride.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather clothing provides the best protection.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious defects.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes are most effective when used together.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from injury in a crash. It also protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles thrown from other vehicles.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have a manual transmission. Shifting to a lower gear slows you down.

questions.question: You should inspect your motorcycle before riding:
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Blend in with traffic so other drivers don't notice you.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce your risk of a crash, be visible to other drivers. Signal your turns and lane changes. Use your brake light and position yourself in the lane so others can see you. Keep distance between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: When riding on bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge grating may cause your motorcycle to weave. This is usually not dangerous. Stay calm and cross at a steady speed. Do not zigzag to avoid the weave, as this is dangerous and takes you out of your lane.

questions.question: Research shows that motorcycles with headlights on during the day are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
Less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on during the day is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on only if it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on when riding, even during the day. This makes you twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: For the best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they don't catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they don't get caught in the motorcycle.

questions.question: When preparing to pass, ride in the left portion of your lane because it:

options.text: Makes it harder to see past the vehicle.
Allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. This improves your view ahead and makes you more visible to drivers in the passing lane.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car:

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
You discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirror. This position helps the driver notice you.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Several surfaces have poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings are all more hazardous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: Only ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only time can lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your body.

questions.question: Motorcycle signals are:

options.text: Even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
Only needed when another vehicle is right next to you.
Less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are more at risk than car and truck drivers. Because of this, using signals correctly on a motorcycle is even more important.

questions.question: Use your turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good protection includes a sturdy jacket, pants that cover your legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift down one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Shift down one gear at a time. Ease out the clutch slowly through the friction zone between each downshift.
